automation.description: Spec format version (default "1", for forward compatibility)

Canonical name. For skills this is the ecosystem identifier — it becomes the skill directory, the SKILL.md frontmatter `name` and therefore the slash command — so it is normalized to ASCII at parse time. For every other type it doubles as the display name.
Display name shown in the UI when `name` is not presentable, i.e. a skill whose author wrote it in a non-ASCII script. Per-locale `i18n` entries take precedence over it.
Human-readable reason for this dependency (shown during install)
Whether this MCP is bundled within the app package

Whether this digital human actually uses the dependency. Optional; absent means enabled. Set to `false` to keep the declaration (and its reason) but stop injecting the MCP for THIS digital human only — a per-app switch that never touches the shared MCP server's own state. The runtime skips `enabled: false` entries (see getMcpServersForRequires).
Skill dependencies (by name/id or structured declaration)
Relative file paths within skills/{id}/ (required when bundled: true)
User configuration schema — rendered as a form during install
Unique key for this config field
Whether the field is required (default: false)
URL-safe unique identifier (single-file: filename, bundle: directory name)
Install provenance: which registry this app was installed from

Install provenance: how this app reached the user's machine. - 'store':   downloaded from a registry (default for store installs) - 'builtin': bundled with the Halo build itself, auto-installed by the built-in loader at startup (see apps/manager/builtin-loader.ts). Built-in apps are protected from permanent deletion and are re-synced from disk on every launch (spec content auto-upgrades with the application; user-controlled state — userConfig, status, overrides — is preserved across upgrades). - 'manual':  added directly via IPC/HTTP without going through the store (e.g. drag-and-drop a SKILL.md file). Older records may not carry this field; treat 'undefined' as 'store' for backwards-compatibility purposes.
Map of option value (as string) → translated label
Per-URL label overrides for browser_login entries
Core system prompt — the "soul" of the automation
Subscription definitions — makes the app "active" in the background
Unique ID within this spec (auto-generated if omitted)
Run only on mainland China working days (holidays and make-up workdays included)
What to watch on the page: "price-element", "full-page", CSS selector, etc.
URL to watch (may be overridden by config_key reference)
Optional: only trigger for specific chat IDs
Frequency bounds (overrides schedule source's own interval for UI adjustment)
Reference to a config_schema key whose value provides dynamic source input
Rule-based event filters (zero LLM cost pre-filtering)
Memory schema — what the AI should track in its memory file
External notification channels to deliver to
Whether AI is allowed to escalate to user (default: true for automation)
Timeout in hours before an unanswered escalation auto-fails (default: 24)
Websites the user needs to log into before the automation can run
URL the user should navigate to for login
Display label for the website (e.g. "小红书")
